clue.text: Defer turning up? Swell

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the little word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a swell is a dandified, upper-class gentleman, a toff

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether delaying an appearance would be a fine idea, with 'swell' as an approving exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an exclamation of approval; it is the noun for a smart gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something off is to postpone it, a phrasal-verb synonym for delaying.

clue.text: Large bra served up in purple

indicators.note: in a down clue, something served up is brought upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: an E fitting is a large bra size
the cup is the part of a bra that names its size

explanation.surface: A generously sized brassiere is presented in a purple shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Together 'Large bra' is an E cup; turned upwards it reads the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Puce is a brownish-purple colour, so it is a specific shade within the purple range.

clue.text: Pinches trophy after taking up bowling like this

indicators.note: once taken up in a down clue, the pair is lifted to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to pinch is to nip
a pot is slang for a sporting trophy cup

explanation.surface: Someone takes up bowling and starts pocketing silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are reversed together, so the trophy ends up at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward rotation put on a ball, a style of delivery in cricket or tennis, so it describes bowling in that way.

clue.text: Almost half of Alcatraz united, enthralled by French bird man?

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so these letters sit inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: first part of the French abbreviation, which wraps the rest

indicators.note: half of an eight-letter word is four letters, and almost that leaves three from the front

parts.note: the first three letters of the prison island's name
people united are as one
the closing letter of FR, the abbreviation for French

explanation.surface: A French connection to the Birdman of Alcatraz, the famous prisoner who kept birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Robert Stroud, the 'Birdman of Alcatraz'. FR, for French, goes around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer trains and flies hawks, so he is jokingly a man whose business is birds.

clue.text: I'm backing competitions engaging student prodigies

indicators.note: going backwards means the contraction before it is read right to left

parts.note: the contraction without its apostrophe

indicators.note: to engage is to take in or hold, so the contests surround the learner

parts.note: races are competitions of speed
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone says they support contests that involve gifted young students.
explanation.walkthrough: The student goes inside the competitions: RAC-L-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigies in the older sense are marvels or wonders, which is what miracles are.

clue.text: One held in jail around city — rough situation?

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so the single letter goes inside the word for jail
around means surrounding, so the jail word also wraps the city's letters

parts.note: to jail someone is to imprison them; this wraps both other pieces
EC is the postcode for the City of London
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An inmate held in a prison in the city is in a rough situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'rough situation' means a state of being rough, not a hardship; jail is the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecision is a lack of exactness, the condition of being only rough or approximate.

clue.text: Disagree, dismissing first total

indicators.note: dismissing the first means sending away the opening letter of the phrase

parts.note: to fall out is to quarrel or disagree

explanation.surface: An argument about getting rid of an opening total.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out effort is complete and total, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Clearly article from Libération's fluently presented without opening line

parts.note: le is a French definite article, as in a French newspaper

indicators.note: without means lacking, and the opening one is the earlier of the two in the word

parts.note: glibly means fluently, with smooth easy talk
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A French newspaper's article is written fluently but lacks its opening line.
explanation.walkthrough: Libération is a French daily newspaper. GLIBLY loses only its first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing legibly means it can be read clearly, so the adverbs share the sense of being plain to read.

clue.text: Marine animal hunting curtailed after receiving text for you

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the shortened word holds the text-speak letter
curtailed means cut short, so the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: hunting is searching
in text messages 'you' is written as the single letter

explanation.surface: A sea creature is hunted until the search is cut short by a text message.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny marine invertebrate, an example of a sea creature.

clue.text: Finished tucking into drink, bowl turned upside-down?

indicators.note: tucking into food puts it inside, so one word sits within the drink

parts.note: cola is a soft drink; it wraps the other piece
when time is up it is finished

explanation.surface: Someone has finished drinking and turns the bowl over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a dome looks like a bowl placed rim-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded dome on a roof, shaped like an inverted bowl.

clue.text: Game soldier from abroad occupying areas, offering defence

indicators.note: troops occupying land sit inside it, so these pieces go inside the two letters

parts.note: A for area; the two of them wrap the rest
polo is a game played on horseback
a GI is an American soldier
the second area

explanation.surface: A brave foreign soldier occupies territory and puts up a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like an adjective meaning plucky; it is the noun naming a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence or justification of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: Equivalent figure in work to advance food additive

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to posit is to put forward or advance an idea
an E number is the code for an approved food additive

explanation.surface: A counterpart at work wants to promote a food additive.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opposite number is the person holding the corresponding post elsewhere, a counterpart.

clue.text: Dicks in orgasm possibly retaining utility

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so the rearranged letters keep the utility word inside
possibly signals that the letters may be arranged in some other way

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
utility means usefulness, use

explanation.surface: A deliberately smutty surface about anatomy and climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicks' here is British slang for idiots, not the anatomical sense the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a dick is a stupid person, and ignoramuses are ignorant people, so both name fools.

clue.text: Government's in better nick, providing digital coverage?

indicators.note: in places this letter within the word for better

parts.note: finer means better; it wraps the next letter
G is the abbreviation for government; the 's is 'is'
to nick a criminal is to catch or nail them

explanation.surface: The Government is in better shape, supplying digital broadcast coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means relating to fingers (digits); 'nick' looks like condition, as in 'good nick', but means arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingernail is the hard plate that covers the tip of a finger, literally a covering for a digit.

clue.text: Female expert gets ready to leave external applications

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an ace is an expert
someone getting ready to leave packs their bags

explanation.surface: An expert woman readies herself to quit, having submitted job applications elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applications' suggests job forms; here they are things applied to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Face packs are creams or pastes spread on the skin of the face, applied externally.

clue.text: Really? That's half gone? It's not true

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Really?'

indicators.note: with half gone only the first two of four letters remain

parts.note: the front half of the word that

explanation.surface: Incredulous chatter: half has disappeared? That's simply not true.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands as a statement: the answer is something that is not true.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a widely held but false belief, a story that is not true.

clue.text: I charge a French body of water to raise this seafood

indicators.note: raising the pieces in a down clue makes them read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to charge at something is to ram it
taken as written
lac is French for lake

explanation.surface: A diner pays to have a French lake dredged for its seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee; it is the verb meaning to butt or ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid prepared as food, usually fried rings, a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Shy about beginning to participate in reproduction

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for shy goes round the single letter

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful; it wraps the next letter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of participate

explanation.surface: A bashful person is reluctant to join in with reproduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' tempts toward breeding; it means a replica.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a reproduction, an imitation made of an original.

clue.text: Joke about artist concealing sex — probably not a favourite of mine!

definitions.text: probably not a favourite of mine!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joke wraps the painter

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words; it wraps everything

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the painter hides the word for sex

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
'it' is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: The setter confesses a liking for risqué jokes and artists who hide sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is allusive: the setter, who puts a smutty clue at 12-down, would hardly be a puritan's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is a person with strict morals who disapproves of sexual jokes, so would dislike this setter.

clue.text: I start to raise it in allotment, producing annoyance

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the word for a share

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of raise
a ration is an allotted share; it wraps the next piece
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener begins growing something on an allotment and annoys the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented plot for growing vegetables in Britain, but here it means an allotted portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritation is the feeling of being annoyed, a direct synonym for annoyance.

clue.text: Seemingly unhappy career amongst those who got elected

indicators.note: amongst puts the word in the middle of the group named next

parts.note: the ins are those in office; this wraps the other piece
to career is to rush along, to tear

explanation.surface: An elected politician whose career looks a misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for one's job; it is the verb meaning to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in tears is crying, which makes them appear unhappy.

clue.text: Month in which daughter never turned up for start of week

indicators.note: in which means inside the month's name, so the other letters go within it

parts.note: the fifth month; it wraps the rest

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
never, as in 'No way!'

explanation.surface: A month in which a daughter failed to show up for the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday is the first working day, the conventional start of the week.

clue.text: Description of theatre and music person creating star, possibly

parts.note: per means for each person, as in 'per head'

indicators.note: possibly suggests that the word is one arrangement among several of its letters

parts.note: forming is creating
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone creating a star is a good description of the theatre and music world.
explanation.definitionFit: The performing arts are the collective term for drama, music and dance performed for an audience.

clue.text: Motor fuel going up, requiring investment of money

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top
an investment puts something inside, so the single letter goes into the reversed fuel

parts.note: oil is a fuel
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Rising fuel costs mean running a car needs more money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motor' looks like an engine; in British slang a motor is a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, or limousine, is a large luxurious car, and motor is informal British for a car.

clue.text: Financial journalists and their boss recalled in unpleasantly sticky surroundings

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the editor's abbreviation is read backwards
surroundings enclose, so the rearranged letters wrap the reversed editor
unpleasantly suggests disorder, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the editor is the boss of journalists

explanation.surface: Financial reporters and their editor are summoned back into a nasty, sticky office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And their boss' looks like part of the definition but is the start of the wordplay. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's city desk is the department covering financial news, and by extension the reporters who staff it.

clue.text: Meat served in American flight mostly spoken about

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word goes round the American flight
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: spoken means said; it wraps the next piece
in US slang 'on the lam' means in flight from the law

explanation.surface: Meat is served on a US flight, and people mostly talk about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel; here it is escape, as in American 'on the lam'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced sausage, a kind of meat.

clue.text: I utter a couple of names when pushing back Hindu beggar

indicators.note: pushing back means moving in the opposite direction, so everything reads right to left

parts.note: to utter is to say, so 'I utter' is 'I say'
N is the abbreviation for name, doubled
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone calls out a few names while pushing back against a Hindu beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sannyasi is a Hindu religious ascetic who has renounced the world and lives by begging.

clue.text: A second firm linked to motor-racing debacle

parts.note: F1, Formula One motor racing, with the 1 as letter I
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A second company tied to motor racing ends in disaster.
